summary_paragraph: John, a homeless man with hypertension and a history of heavy alcohol use, was readmitted after returning with palpitations and inability to walk, found to be in atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate. He was treated with metoprolol and diltiazem to control his heart rate, then transitioned to once-daily Toprol XL and aspirin for stroke prevention. His chest pain was evaluated and deemed non-cardiac, likely musculoskeletal. He showed no signs of alcohol withdrawal during this admission but was counseled on the risks of continued drinking, which exacerbates his atrial fibrillation. Liver enzymes were elevated consistent with alcohol use, but no acute intervention was needed. He was discharged home with prescriptions sent to a care pharmacy and advised to follow up with services for the homeless. He left medically stable with controlled heart rate and clear mental status.
